clue.text: Stop paper using old army signalling equipment

parts.note: in cricket, to field is to stop the ball
the Daily Telegraph is a British newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone halts a newspaper that relied on antique military communications kit.
explanation.walkthrough: To field in cricket is to stop the ball before it reaches the boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable wire-based telegraph set up near the front lines was the army's means of sending messages in older wars.

clue.text: Get really cross at barber's carelessness!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to rage furiously, like a mad dog
second meaning, taken literally: a careless barber leaves shaving lather on your lips

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a playful literal reading: a sloppy barber's shaving lather ends up on the customer's lips.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone so furious they seem to be frothing like a rabid animal.

clue.text: Arise from name brought up at first encounter

indicators.note: in a down entry, bringing something up reads it from bottom to top
at first points to the opening letter of the following word only

explanation.surface: Something springs from a name mentioned at a first meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate from a source is to issue or originate from it, a synonym of arise from.

clue.text: Aid to cleanliness to put a chap off?

wordplay.note: to put off is to deter, and a chap is a gent, written one after the other

explanation.surface: A cleaning product so strong it might repel a man.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as two words: DETER (put off) and GENT (chap); the phrase 'put off' wraps round 'a chap' but the letters simply follow on.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergent is a washing agent used in cleaning clothes and dishes, so it assists cleanliness.

clue.text: Observe with gravity girl through telescope, perhaps

definitions.note: the eyeglass is the lens one looks through on a telescope

parts.note: G is the symbol for gravity

explanation.surface: An astronomer and a girl solemnly peering through a telescope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gravity' looks like seriousness but supplies the physics symbol G.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeglass is the lens fitted at the viewing end of an optical instrument such as a telescope.

clue.text: Gain by violence from old wrong

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Profiting by force from an ancient injustice.
explanation.walkthrough: A tort is the legal term for a civil wrong such as negligence.
explanation.definitionFit: To extort is to obtain money or favours through threats or force.

clue.text: Motown singer to love Italian red

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A soul singer declares a fondness for Italian wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosso is the Italian word for the colour red, also used of red wine.

clue.text: Wan child in loose overcoat

parts.note: a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A sickly-looking youngster wrapped in a baggy coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A paletot is a French-style loose outer coat or jacket for men or women.

clue.text: Utter immorality spoils man as high flier

parts.note: to air a view is to utter it

explanation.surface: Sheer wickedness is ruining a fellow who aims to rise high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High flier' sounds like an ambitious person, but it is literal: a senior officer in an air force.
explanation.definitionFit: An air vice-marshal is a senior rank in the Royal Air Force, whose officers fly aircraft.

clue.text: By arrangement meant some to enter flat

indicators.note: entering means going inside something else
an arrangement sets things out in a new order

parts.note: some is a part of the whole

explanation.surface: By agreement, some people were supposed to move into a flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Apartment is the usual American word for a flat, a set of rooms in a larger building.

clue.text: Sun turns it into a good conductor

indicators.note: turning round makes a word face the other way

explanation.surface: The sun makes something into a good conductor of heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good conductor' suggests physics, but it is a person: Sir Georg Solti led orchestras.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Georg Solti was a celebrated Hungarian-British orchestral maestro, so he is a fine example of a musical director.

clue.text: Robin's song with modern tune?

definitions.note: the song is titled Robin Adair, so the answer completes it

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era

explanation.surface: A bird's song given a contemporary melody.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin is not the bird: Robin Adair is an old Irish ballad, and the answer is the second word of its title.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional song 'Robin Adair' takes its title from the man's name, so the answer is that surname.

clue.text: The French marine "not out 0" against the Russian poet

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of order

parts.note: the figure zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A French marine, unbeaten on nought, batting against a Russian poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not out 0' reads like a cricket score but splits into an anagram of 'not' and the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikhail Lermontov was a nineteenth-century Romantic writer, author of A Hero of Our Time.

clue.text: Article about ancient city by head teacher (No.666)

indicators.note: the city name is placed about, that is around, the word before it

parts.note: Thebes was a city of ancient Egypt and Greece

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece on an old city, written by a headmistress.
explanation.walkthrough: The article A sits inside THEBES before the S; 666 is the number of the beast in the Book of Revelation.
explanation.definitionFit: In Revelation the beast's number is given as six hundred threescore and six, so the figure identifies that creature.

clue.text: Raincoat with its inside messed up with putty

indicators.note: inside places one thing within another

parts.note: a mac is a mackintosh, a raincoat

indicators.note: messing something up puts it into disorder

explanation.surface: A raincoat whose lining has been ruined by putty.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastic is a resin-based paste used as a filler or sealant, much like putty.

clue.text: Plant meets disaster in song

indicators.note: in places one thing within another

parts.note: an aria is a song in opera

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things in chaos and out of order

explanation.surface: A plant comes to grief during a song.
explanation.walkthrough: The usual spelling is artemisia; this grid uses the variant with E.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemisia is a genus of aromatic shrubs including wormwood and tarragon.

clue.text: Great beast seen by the two people round eastern border

indicators.note: round places one thing around another

parts.note: both means the two of them
a hem is the border of cloth

explanation.surface: A huge creature spotted by a couple near the eastern frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Behemoth is the giant creature of the Book of Job, now used for anything enormous.

clue.text: Condition found in forest at eventide

indicators.note: found in says the letters are already sitting within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something discovered in the woods at dusk.
explanation.walkthrough: Estate in the old sense of a person's condition or standing, as in 'man's estate'.
explanation.definitionFit: Estate can mean a state or condition of life, a dated sense still seen in phrases like the estate of matrimony.

clue.text: Political opportunist has apparently lost weight

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who trims sails to the wind, changing views for advantage

definitions.note: a comparative adjective; the clue phrases it as a description
definitions.meaning: second meaning: more slender than before

explanation.walkthrough: The 'apparently' warns that the second half is read as a comparative adjective: someone looking slimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimmer historically was a politician who shifted allegiance with circumstances; trimmer also means slimmer.

clue.text: Top child turn has fitting round back

indicators.note: round places one thing around another
going back means running the other way

parts.note: a tot is a small child
a U-turn, so U for turn

explanation.surface: A toddler doing a turn wears a properly fitted garment back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like a garment or the summit, but it is the spinning toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotum is a small spinning toy with lettered sides, a kind of top used in games of chance.

clue.text: Agrees with point composer accepts

indicators.note: accepting something takes it in

parts.note: Thomas Tallis was an English Tudor composer

explanation.surface: A composer goes along with a suggestion he takes on board.
explanation.definitionFit: If one account tallies with another, the two correspond or agree.

clue.text: Weapon standard rising? That's right!

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising reads a word from the bottom upwards

parts.note: i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a flag going up is right, and is told it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' is i.e., the abbreviation for 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapier is a slender thrusting sword used in duelling.

clue.text: Eastern tea mixture helps one to find one's bearings

indicators.note: a mixture stirs its ingredients together into a new order

explanation.surface: An Oriental tea blend that helps you get your bearings.
explanation.definitionFit: To orientate oneself is to work out where one is and which way to go.

clue.text: Remarks of a financial nature, perhaps

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as financial remarks, but the second sense is banknotes, money itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes are brief comments, and notes are also pieces of paper currency.

clue.text: Behold the animal's swallowing back tooth!

indicators.note: going back means running the other way
swallowing takes something inside

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Look! The creature is gulping down a back tooth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back tooth' reads as a single phrase, but 'back' reverses the wordplay and 'tooth' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A molar is one of the broad grinding teeth at the rear of the mouth.

clue.text: Encountered backward training test

indicators.note: backward means running the other way

explanation.surface: A test met during a remedial training course.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempt in its older sense means to try or put to the proof, as in tempting fate.

clue.text: Forger makes this minor change

indicators.note: a change reworks the letters into something different

explanation.surface: A counterfeiter makes a small alteration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forger' suggests a fraudster, but here it is a metalworker who forges iron.
explanation.definitionFit: A smith works metal at a forge, shaping hot iron by hammering it.

clue.text: Listens to Lear rambling outside after order for final run through

parts.note: to dress ranks is to put soldiers in order

indicators.note: outside places one thing around another
rambling wanders off course, out of order

explanation.surface: Someone attends to King Lear's wandering speech after a command, at the last practice.
explanation.walkthrough: To dress, in military drill, is to bring soldiers into straight lines.
explanation.definitionFit: The dress rehearsal is the last full practice of a play, in costume, before opening night.
